source: Two screenshots of a battery diagnostic tool, supplied by the owner as reference
controlled_variables_unchanged: cell voltage (3.938 V), current (0), temperature (23.3 C)
interpretation: Qmax (chemical capacity) is identical in A and B while the reported actual/full-charge capacity falls by 371 mAh. The displayed capacity loss is therefore a reversible charge-limit effect, not chemical ageing. A separate 4.08 V UI reading appears identically in both screenshots; per the owner it is a current battery-level reading and is irrelevant to this comparison.
limits_note_4_08v: Owner-confirmed: the 4.08 V item is a current battery level/voltage reading, not a configured limit. It is identical in both conditions and is excluded from the A/B analysis.
relevance_to_iphone_01: The iPhone 17 nameplate top band is 4500 mV and the extrapolated >=1000 band is 4390 mV, i.e. the exact same 110 mV span. This makes the measured slope a directly relevant empirical calibration for the voltage-node capacity cost, in place of generic estimates.
limitations: Different device/capacity (4630 mAh vs 3692 mAh); slope is applied as a percentage, assuming similar OCV shape on the same 4.50 V platform.
The 4390 mV reading was set on a diagnostic tool, not observed as an iOS-configured limit on iphone-01.
Single A/B pair, single battery; no error bars.
The 4.08 V reading is a current battery-level value (owner-confirmed), identical in both conditions, and excluded from analysis.
